n: The heading places David in a cave, hiding from Saul. He takes shelter under God’s wings, like a chick under its mother, until the danger passes.

f.w: in the shadow of thy wings

n: He cries to God Most High, who will complete his purpose for David.
God will reach down from heaven and rescue him, sending his loyal love and faithfulness like messengers.

f.g: God’s ḥesed and faithfulness, pictured as two angels sent to help.

n: David lies down among lion-like men who breathe fire, whose teeth are weapons and whose tongues are sharp swords.
A refrain repeated in verse 11: may God be lifted high above the heavens and his glory fill the earth. In the middle of danger, David thinks of God’s greatness.

f.w: let thy glory be above all the earth

n: They set a net and dug a pit for him — and fell into it themselves.

f.w: into the midst whereof they are fallen themselves

n: “My heart is fixed” — steady and firm. Despite everything, he will sing. Verses 7–11 reappear as the opening of Psalm 108.
He calls his own soul and his instruments to wake up — he will wake the dawn itself with praise.
He will praise God not only in Israel but among all the nations.
God’s loyal love reaches the heavens and his faithfulness the clouds.

f.w: thy mercy is great unto the heavens

n: The refrain closes the psalm: God be exalted above the heavens, your glory over all the earth.
